premises.text: Heavy industries need heat that is cheap, reliable, and flame-hot, but zero-carbon options today fail that combination and become unaffordable when made reliable
premises.evidence_span: There is no affordable way to decarbonize our heavy industries

premises.text: The Joule Hive thermal battery takes cheap abundant electricity, stores it as heat, and delivers hot gas to existing furnaces, boilers, and kilns
premises.evidence_span: This system takes in electricity from renewables or off-peak nuclear or hydro whenever it's cheap, whenever it's abundant, whenever it's available

premises.text: The system reaches 1,800 Celsius heat at least three times cheaper than hydrogen while remaining retrofittable to existing processes
premises.evidence_span: we can keep it affordable, at least three times cheaper than hydrogen. And best of all, we're retrofitable

premises.text: Electrically conductive fire bricks (e-bricks) made from doped refractory materials go hotter and last longer than today's electric heaters
premises.evidence_span: We use semiconductor doping to make them electrically conductive. The result is a material that can go hotter and last longer than electric heaters today

premises.text: Stacked e-bricks form a three-in-one electric heater, thermal store, and heat exchanger from cheap abundant bricks
premises.evidence_span: It's a giant electric heater. It's a giant thermal store. And it's a giant heat exchanger that gets the energy out, all built from cheap, affordable, abundant bricks

premises.text: In markets with cheap renewable electricity, the system can pay back in about five years while offsetting most carbon emissions, or beat electric boilers on time-of-use rates
premises.evidence_span: We can pay back in five years while offsetting 80% of your carbon emissions

value.text: Affordable, reliable, flame-hot electrified heat that decarbonizes heavy industry without radically changing existing processes
value.evidence_span: turn the power from those sources into reliable industrial heat

secondary_value.text: Decarbonize industrial sites and offset carbon emissions

causal_links.evidence_span: We stack these up to massive scales to build our dual high thermal battery
we need a new approach to decarbonize our heat
deliver it to your furnace, to your boiler, to your kiln, in place of the fossil fuels you usually burn
Electricity prices, we see that in the Midwest, you can operate in areas today where 50% of the year, electricity is cheaper than natural gas

notes: Scale-up demo (pellets to towers) treated as evidence of feasibility, not separate premises. 'Industry electrified by 2045' vision not coded as premise (§4.1(4)). Heat/cost/retrofit kept as one commercial performance premise with e-brick as separately revisable materials module. Singleton D1 and D3 justified as market-need and deployment-economics modules.
